title: A second drone attack on Bahrain, a Hamas commander killed, and a retreat at the mouth of the Red Sea
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim a second drone attack on a US radar in Bahrain and Bahrain says it shot the drones down, another tanker is attacked in the Gulf, Israel kills the commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, Saudi-backed forces in Yemen pull back from the Bab el-Mandeb strait, Russian strikes hit Chornomorsk and Zaporizhzhia, and the carrier Theodore Roosevelt is reported about to join two others in the Middle East.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Sunday, November fifteenth. And for the second time in three days, Iran says it has attacked an American military site in Bahrain.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: This time, Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six drones targeted a US air-defence radar at Riffa Air Base. They called it the second phase of their response to what they describe as American aggression.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And Bahrain's account?

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Bahrain Defence Force says its air defences intercepted and destroyed the drones before they reached their targets. US Central Command hadn't confirmed any damage or casualties when this was reported.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So it's the same pattern as Friday. Then, the Guards claimed they had destroyed an early-warning radar, and Central Command said it shot down two drones with no damage at all.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. On the map, both attacks are recorded as intercepted. But two attempts in three days is a real change. Before Friday, Iran hadn't tried to hit a military site in a Gulf state for more than two months, according to CNN.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And it comes right after President Trump said he'd strike Iran again with no hesitation if it threatened American allies or ships. That's the thing to watch.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: At sea, the attacks on tankers continue. The British maritime agency UKMTO, citing Indian shipping authorities, reported an attack on a tanker heading east through the Gulf, toward the Strait of Hormuz. The crew is safe. The damage isn't known.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, separately, that two tankers were on fire after hitting mines. As with all of those mine claims, it hasn't been confirmed. The Guards also insisted the strait remains closed, and claimed American efforts to escort ships through it have failed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Staying in the region, there's a significant development in Gaza. Israel and Hamas have both confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, the commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, was killed in an Israeli strike.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It happened just after midnight on Saturday, in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis. The Nasser Medical Complex says the strike killed one person and wounded two. Al Jazeera reports it hit a tent sheltering displaced people.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Who was he? Hamas's armed wing described him as a member of its general military council, and said he was among the commanders who planned the October seventh attack. Israel says he directed attacks on Israeli civilians and troops. His predecessor was killed in September.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So that's two commanders of the same brigade killed in two months.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the wider toll keeps rising despite the ceasefire. Gaza's Health Ministry counted sixteen people killed and sixty-eight injured over forty-eight hours.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now to Yemen, where there's a shift on the ground that matters for shipping. Reuters reports that the Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces have pulled back from the area around Dhubab and the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the narrow passage at the southern end of the Red Sea. The forces moved to a position about a hundred and fifty kilometres west of Aden, and said they'd focus on securing Aden and the governorates around it.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Reuters describes it as the apparent end of a six-week counteroffensive against the Houthis. Neither the Houthis nor Saudi Arabia commented. We haven't changed the Houthi areas on the map yet, because it isn't confirmed who now holds that ground.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Meanwhile, the missiles keep coming. The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh this morning, plus drones over the Eastern Province. No damage or casualties were reported.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Officials say at least twenty-six people have been killed in suspected Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia since late September.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's turn to Ukraine. Overnight, a Russian strike hit Chornomorsk, the port town near Odesa. Ukraine's emergency service says six people were injured. Energy infrastructure was damaged, a four-storey administrative building was wrecked, and a gas pipeline was ruptured.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And on Saturday evening, regional officials say Russian aircraft dropped twelve guided bombs on Zaporizhzhia. Six civilians were wounded, including a two-year-old. Traffic across the big hydroelectric dam on the Dnipro was closed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the same city where strikes on Friday killed two people and injured fifty. And the grid operator reported emergency power cuts in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: President Zelensky put a number on the week. He says Russia launched more than two thousand three hundred drones, one thousand five hundred and ninety guided bombs, and fifteen missiles at Ukraine in seven days.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line, some better news for Kyiv. The Institute for the Study of War assessed that Ukrainian forces recently advanced south of Novopavlivka and east of Oleksandrivka. Russian attacks toward Kupiansk, Borova and Dobropillia on Friday and Saturday made no gains.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the Institute repeated its warning about Kostiantynivka. It says the local ceasefire Russia is seeking there would likely help it reinforce the southern side of Ukraine's fortress belt.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On diplomacy, one small step. Kyiv Post reports Jared Kushner saying the US is working on direct contacts between Moscow and European governments before the next round of talks. There's still no date for that round.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Finally, the ships, and this one's worth noting. The news agency APA, citing the New York Times, reports that the carrier Theodore Roosevelt is due to join the George H. W. Bush and the George Washington in the Middle East tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That would put three American carriers in the region at once, though the Roosevelt is expected to relieve the George Washington, which has been there since August. The Navy hasn't confirmed the arrival, so on the map we've moved the Roosevelt to an estimated position on the approach to the Arabian Sea. Monday's fleet tracker should confirm it.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, what to watch. Whether Washington responds to two Iranian attempts on Bahrain. The Roosevelt's arrival, and how long three carriers stay together. Who moves into the ground near Bab el-Mandeb. And a date for the Ukraine talks and the prisoner exchange.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
